post.originalText:
Okay, this time motion designers might actually be fully cooked.

Saw people saying Opus 5.5 can do real motion design and I did not buy it. Looked like another AI demo that falls apart after 3 seconds.

So I tested it on a @PayBox logo. One prompt. Ten seconds. It spat this back in one pass.

I did not even explain what PayBox does. The agent read the logo, found the product, figured out the company, and wrote the scenario itself.

This is code. No After Effects. No editor sitting on the timeline for a week.

A studio would quote days and a few thousand for a brand sting like this. The model just built the cube, landed the lockup, and moved on.

Vision does not save you here either. The model is already overtrained on this look, and X is full of examples. Realistically, you do not need an experienced creative in the loop. You need a logo and one sentence.

The only part still on us is what to ask for. Prompt below.

@amfonte @PayBox That's indeed a labeled reel. The key thing here is the price. This work is now one prompt and 3% of a $20 subscription.

A person can still make a great output that actually explains PayBox and does not look like a "white labeled reel". Most buyers will still take the cheapest option that ships tonight. Cost and speed are now part of quality, not just the animation.
